subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public synchronous config-write veto hook, and what trust, ordering, and failure contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the hook would let plugins block persistent config writes across auth, provider, SecretRef, startup, and reload surfaces; automation cannot safely choose that public security boundary.

options.title: Design narrow config-write hook
options.body: Define a config-specific plugin/API contract with current and pending config, action, changed paths, actor metadata, base hash, typed rejection, timeouts, recursion protection, and regression tests.

options.title: Fold into durable-write hook
options.body: Make this a config-specific case of the broader before-persistence-write design, accepting a larger cross-state API discussion before this issue is implemented.

options.title: Reject plugin veto
options.body: Keep config safety in built-in validation, doctor, rollback, and allowlists only, and document that plugins cannot synchronously block core config writes.

recommendation.title: Design narrow config-write hook
recommendation.body: Define a config-specific plugin/API contract with current and pending config, action, changed paths, actor metadata, base hash, typed rejection, timeouts, recursion protection, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion already includes steipete's review keeping this open and the current central source lines trace to the same recent area history.
